_comment: WHATSAPP IVR FLOW — the agreed two-door tree, in the chat.
Needs cafex-backend at or after ec20bd3c ("nested IVR menus of unlimited
depth, config-driven"). Menus below the root live in `nodes`; a button
opens one with `next`; __BACK__ and __HOME__ navigate and are honoured only
in the node that lists them. No backend code is changed by this file.
THIS FILE IS THE TOP LEVEL ONLY. The live whatsappIvrFlow also carries a
`roles` block — WHOLESALER_ADMIN, WHOLESALER_AGENT, RETAILER_PRIMARY,
PRIVATE_USER — which belongs to the platform, not to this file. When pasting:
replace the top-level keys, add `staticLinkMessage` and `nodes`, and leave
`roles` exactly as it is. Pasting this file over the whole object would
delete every registered user's menu.
A registered user whose role is listed there sees their role menu and never
this tree. They inherit `nodes` and `staticLinkMessage` from here but cannot
reach either — their buttons are smart links and support, never `url` or
`next`.
<BASE> — the published v7 root, e.g.
https://nishant-devekar.github.io/foodbridge-mock-platform/v7
The simulator at v7/ivr.html substitutes its own origin.
THE TREE
Hi ─┬─ I'm new here ──── Shall I set up your business on this number?
│                        ├─ Yes, set it up  → link: sign up
│                        └─ Not now ─────── pick a feature → link
├─ I have an account ─ Do you run a store, or buy from one?
│                        ├─ I run a store ── Business options
│                        │     ├─ FoodBridge Recommends ── what needs you → link
│                        │     └─ orders · collections · inventory · purchase · support
│                        └─ I buy from one ── orders · shop · a problem
└─ Talk to a person
STATIC LINKS ONLY. A caller the backend does not recognise always gets the
top-level flow — and so does a registered user whose role has no entry
under `roles` — and a smart link needs a resolved user, so every leaf of
this tree is a fixed `url`. Nothing substitutes into a url, which is why a
brand-new visitor types their number once on sign-up.
LIMITS, per menu — root and every node alike: 10 buttons at most (Meta
rejects more and buildMenuReply does not cap them); 3 or fewer draw reply
buttons, more draw a list. Titles 20 (reply) / 24 (list), descriptions 72.
EVERY NODE HAS A WAY BACK. Back buttons are not injected — a node without
__BACK__ or __HOME__ holds the user until the 30-minute session timeout.
NO {userName} OUTSIDE THE GREETING. An unrecognised caller's name is the
orchestrator's fallback, "there" — right in "Hello there!", wrong in
"Got it, there." This tree is mostly walked by unrecognised callers.
NO RUPEE FIGURES. This tenant's export has orders but no invoices or
payments (D-015); rows promise cadence and work, never cash.
RECOMMENDS CARRIES NO COUNTS. The drawing it comes from reads "5 orders
delayed, ₹1,24,000 pending collections". A config string cannot be live: the
count would be right on the day it was pasted and wrong in the room a week
later, beside a control tower that computes it fresh. And the rupee figure is
one this tenant cannot support (D-015). So the chat names what needs
attention and the link shows how much — the number lives where it is live.
FIVE WORDS OR FEWER, EVERYWHERE (20 Sep 2026, product owner). No row carries a
description and no greeting carries a second line: someone should read a
message at a glance and know what to tap. The {title} a link message quotes
is the row just tapped, so it is not counted against the line around it.
